target.title: fix(zalo): add timeouts to Bot API requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users sending Zalo messages, photos, chat actions, or webhook configuration requests could wait indefinitely when the Zalo Bot API accepted the request or sent headers but then stopped responding.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Zalo Bot API client now applies a 30s default request deadline to normal API calls while still honoring explicit per-call timeouts. The existing `getUpdates` long-poll path continues to pass its own `(poll timeout + 5s)` deadline, and the existing media SSRF guard and bounded JSON response reader remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Zalo send and webhook operations now fail with an abort instead of hanging forever on a network black hole. Long polling keeps its current timeout behavior, so polling waits are not shortened by the new default request deadline.

## Evidence

Base: upstream/main `3ec2a50d6c0a62a484e630536c658a8357e4e211`
Head: `e94b507c98` (`fix(zalo): add timeouts to Bot API requests`)

- `node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs warmup --provider blacksmith-testbox --keep --timing-json` - blocked before remote execution: selected `crabbox` binary failed basic `--version`/`--help` sanity checks.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/zalo/src/api.test.ts` - passed after rebasing to latest upstream/main, 1 file / 19 tests.
- `TMPDIR=/media/vdc/0668001470/tmp/openclaw-zalo-test-tmp node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <all 23 extensions/zalo/src/*.test.ts files>` - passed before the latest rebase, 23 files / 115 tests.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental false --pretty false` - passed before the latest rebase.
- `oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/zalo/src/api.ts extensions/zalo/src/api.test.ts` - passed after rebasing to latest upstream/main.
- `oxlint --threads=1 extensions/zalo/src/api.ts extensions/zalo/src/api.test.ts` - passed after rebasing to latest upstream/main.
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` - passed after rebasing to latest upstream/main.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main --engine claude` - clean, no accepted/actionable findings before the latest rebase; the rebase was conflict-free and only moved the same patch onto latest main.

Note: the first full Zalo test run failed because this local machine has a root-owned `/tmp/openclaw-test-state`, causing unrelated SQLite hosted-media tests to hit EACCES. Re-running the same Zalo test set with a writable `TMPDIR` passed.


## Native Fetch Controlled-Server Timeout Proof

Current head: `e94b507c98d82a28b0346c7b900e81411fd2a224`

This proof used a local controlled HTTP server on `127.0.0.1` with a fake redacted token and no Zalo credentials or external API calls. The client path used native Node `fetch` through the real Zalo API client.

Focused regression test:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-zalo.config.ts extensions/zalo/src/api.test.ts --reporter=verbose
Result: passed, 1 file / 19 tests.
```

Controlled-server runtime output:

```text
proof-start: head=e94b507c98d82a28b0346c7b900e81411fd2a224 transport="native Node fetch" apiUrl="http://127.0.0.1:<redacted-port>" token="<redacted-token>"
normal-success getMe: elapsedMs=41 resultSummary=ok
server-stalled-body sendMessage: headers sent; body intentionally held open
ordinary stalled sendMessage default deadline: elapsedMs=30005 errorName=AbortError errorMessage="This operation was aborted"
server-stalled-body getUpdates: headers sent; body intentionally held open
long-poll stalled getUpdates timeout=45: elapsedMs=50001 errorName=AbortError errorMessage="This operation was aborted"
```

Summary:

```json
{
  "ordinaryExpectedMs": 30000,
  "longPollExpectedMs": 50000,
  "ordinaryWithinTolerance": true,
  "longPollWithinTolerance": true,
  "noExternalZaloCredentials": true
}
```

Deadline rationale: the Zalo client already treats `getUpdates` as long polling with a 30-second default poll timeout and a request deadline of `poll timeout + 5s`. This patch gives ordinary API calls the same bounded 30-second default so stalled fetch/body reads return control instead of hanging indefinitely, while preserving explicit long-poll behavior. The controlled-server proof shows ordinary calls abort at about 30s and `getUpdates({ timeout: 45 })` still gets the explicit 50s deadline.
